messages:
sarah-ops: Heads up — APAC users saw intermittent 503s on model-proxy starting ~08:22 UTC, looks correlated with mTLS handshake failures.

maria-infra: pulling proxy logs now, can you paste an example error?

sarah-ops: example from proxy logs:
```
2026-03-22T08:22:09Z proxy[fwk]: tls_handshake_error: remote error: tls: unknown certificate
caused_by: keystore unwrap failed: kms.DecryptAccessDenied: Access denied for role arn:aws:iam::111:role/proxy-keystore-apac
```

raj-sec: KMS Decrypt denied — did we roll any RBAC or IAM denies to APAC recently? @maria-infra

maria-infra: yes, PR #4123 applied a deny-focused policy at 07:50 to reduce cross-account Decrypt surface. It was rolled incrementally to ap-southeast-1.

jon-oncall: keystore fetches failing => mTLS client cert validation fails => 503s. I'm going to pause rollout to other regions.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-20260322-APAC-MTLS (P1) — responders: jon-oncall, maria-infra, raj-sec

maria-infra: grep shows ~14% of ap-southeast-1 ingress proxies saw repeated kms:DecryptAccessDenied between 08:21–08:30. other regions unaffected.

raj-sec: please pull CloudTrail events for the role and that time range; check whether deny is from a Service Control Policy, permission boundary, or explicit IAM deny. Also grab agent audit logs for the proxy principal.

sarah-ops: CloudTrail excerpt:
```
EventTime: 2026-03-22T08:22:09Z
EventName: Decrypt
Principal: arn:aws:sts::111:assumed-role/proxy-keystore-apac/i-0a1b2c
ResponseElements: {"ErrorCode":"AccessDenied"}
```

jon-oncall: confirmed Decrypt AccessDenied. Short mitigation: enable regional keystore caching for a short TTL to avoid KMS calls while we fix the policy. Can someone flip the cache feature flag?

maria-infra: toggling feature flag: `ff toggle proxy.keystore.cache.apac true` now.

sarah-ops: after enabling cache, 503s dropped from ~12% to ~1% within 3 minutes. good temporary recovery. :thumbsup:

raj-sec: need root cause. @maria-infra paste the policy diff applied in PR #4123.

maria-infra: excerpt of diff:
```
-    "Action": "kms:Decrypt",
-    "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-1:111:key/keystore",
+    "NotAction": ["kms:List*","kms:Describe*"],
+    "Effect": "Deny",
```

maria-infra: tl;dr: we introduced a deny-by-default block and missed explicitly allowing the proxy-keystore role. my mistake.

raj-sec: Deny precedence explains the failures. Action items: 1) patch policy to allow proxy-keystore Decrypt for ap-southeast-1; 2) add preflight Decrypt simulation to policy rollout CI; 3) forward KMS CloudTrail events to SIEM for immediate alerting; 4) update incident runbook to include cache-flip mitigation.

jon-oncall: applying temporary policy patch to restore kms:Decrypt for `proxy-keystore-apac` now.

infra-bot: Policy patch deploy started — change id: patch-20260322-01

jon-oncall: patch applied. KMS Decrypt calls succeed, keystore unwraps working, mTLS handshakes recovered. switching to monitoring.

sarah-ops: postmortem items: missed allow-list entry, deny-style policy without exhaustive allowlist, absent preflight tests, cache-flip saved traffic.

raj-sec: additional recommendations: CI rule that assumes the affected role and runs a dry-run Decrypt against the target key; tighter PR review checklist for deny policies; and an automated alert rule in SIEM for KMS Decrypt AccessDenied spikes. I'll draft a proposal.

maria-infra: filed followups: infra-2462 (preflight Decrypt simulation), infra-2463 (policy rollout canary + checklist), infra-2464 (forward CloudTrail KMS events to SIEM).

sarah-ops: owners: maria -> infra-2462+2463, raj -> infra-2464, jon -> update runbook with cache-flip snippet. ETA: 1 week for initial fixes?

jon-oncall: ACK. Playbook snippet I'm adding to runbook:
```
1) ff toggle proxy.keystore.cache.apac true
2) verify cached serving via /_health/keystore on a few hosts
3) apply policy patch or rollback PR
4) monitor KMS Decrypt metrics and keystore unwrap success for 30m
```

sec-bot: Linked playbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/mTLS-keystore-fallback

sarah-ops: closing incident thread here. will collect detailed timeline and writeup in the postmortem doc. thanks all. :raised_hands:
